about: Law and enforcement package data for the outfits system (Saint Jude). Numbers are figure keys in design_figures.json (Design proposals). priority: lower is first in line for an ordinary crime in that jurisdiction. Sources: Part II 3.4 (what the Pad cannot buy), Part II 2.7, Part IV 2.7 and 4.4.

agency_routing.note: A street matter goes to the precinct that covers the place (the SJPD where none does); an organized-crime matter to the OCCD; a place inside a county jurisdiction's own location to that county's prosecutor; a federal matter to the FBI, a racket to the Strike Force. Unsourced routing.
agency_routing.bribery_fraud_note: Part II 4.5 and 5: the State Commission of Investigation (the state_ag profile stands for it: it can subpoena and hold hearings but cannot prosecute) takes bribery inside the city; fraud goes to the FBI; a federal bribery matter to the Strike Force. Unsourced beyond the agencies' names.

office_domains.note: occupation domain of the person who sits in an office; soldier is the engine's word for a sworn officer

no_woman_note: Part I 11: no woman has been mayor, police commissioner, County Prosecutor or union president on the docks; the Teamsters seat is added by analogy (unsourced)

arrangements.note: Part II 2.1: the SJPD is overwhelmingly white, male and Catholic, so officers are drawn from the city's white ethnic groups at their weights; the captain tier's first seat in each precinct is the precinct captain, the rest are lieutenants and detective heads. Ages and tier titles are unsourced.

response.about: How a crime becomes a report, a case, an arrest, a disposition and a sentence (task B13). Every figure is a Design proposal with its reasoning; none is a cap, a quota or a fixed share. Real-world rates are calibration targets reported after a run: most cases end in a plea or are dropped, mob cases went to trial more often (bible Part II 6.5: most cases end in a plea; a made man typically refuses to plead if it requires naming others). A logistic term is a weighed pressure (z = bias + sum of coefficient x input), never a threshold.

harm.why: A harm row whose intent is hostile or lethal, and an accidental one that names an offender (a bystander hit), is a crime someone could report. Controlled harm (sport) and plain accidents are not.

publicity.why: Publicity is 0..100 = 100 * (1 - product(1 - weight_i * x_i)) over the drivers, so each adds and none can exceed the whole. It is the starting value of a report's public attention; the information layer later makes it grow or fade. Part II 3.4 (the Pad cannot make a public killing go away) is why a public killing, a bystander hit or a killed officer scores high; the weights are proposals.
publicity.place_crowd_why: Expected people within sight at the busiest hour (unsourced).
publicity.place_exposure_why: How open the place is to the street's eyes, 0..1 (unsourced).
publicity.hour_weights_why: Relative chance a crime is committed in each hour, 0 to 23 (more by day and early evening; unsourced).
publicity.hour_exposure_why: How many people are about in each hour, 0..1: a dark small hour against a lunchtime street (unsourced).
publicity.method_why: How loud the method is, 0..1: a shot at range is heard and seen, a quiet disappearance is neither (unsourced).

officer.why: A killed or hurt officer is the department's own and every agency answers it.

office_holder.why: A man who holds a public office or a seat the world tracks as an office.

inducted.why: A made man's killing is news to the families and the Organized Crime unit even when the street is quiet.

identification.why: The harm record names the true offender; the law only has him once someone has put the name to the crime. At filing it is a weighed chance (logistic): those who saw it and a loud story raise it, a made man's work and a victim from the same world (the street keeps its mouth shut) lower it. Targets read from memory of 1975, approximate and flagged so: about a half to three-fifths of assaults reported to police were cleared, most killings overall (a bit under four in five) were cleared, but a killing inside organised crime almost never was. Targets only, never caps; the roll's drivers are what move the result. Reviews can still name him later.

review_rate.why: Per review of an open case, the chance the work puts a name to the crime, times the agency's effort (a case is reviewed about every two weeks and closed after three months).

sweep.why: A killing the police take hard brings a sweep (B12f): a pressure from the report (how public, how hot the outfits, how much the agency can do, an officer killed), then a number of men around a mean the pressure raises, picked by how close each stands to the killer. The men are held a few days and a joint case names them as co-defendants. Unsourced; the Bureau and the SJPD did sweep after a killing that made the papers (bible Part II 6, 7).

evidence.why: Part 2's formula 0.3 + 0.4*public + 0.2*known, with public now the weighed publicity share (0..1), plus the effort the agency puts in; seeded noise of +-noise. Unsourced.

default_threshold.why: The threshold for a crime kind the rules above do not list (unsourced).

effort.why: How hard an agency works a case, 0..1 = capacity * (1 - product(1 - weight*x)): a front-page story and a killed officer bring every agency (a weight on effort and reach). Unsourced.

arrangements.why: The chance the Pad buries a case it reaches is (1 - resist), resist = 1 - (1 - publicity_resistance*publicity)(1 - officer_victim_resistance*officer). At full publicity the Pad all but cannot bury it (Part II 3.4: it cannot make a public killing go away) but the weight stays below 1: the evidence still has to exist. Unsourced values.

arrest.officer_roles_why: Who is likely to catch a case in a precinct (the opening has no detectives, so the supervising ranks and the patrol stand in; unsourced).

review.why: What a review of an open case adds to its evidence, scaled by effort (unsourced).

bail.why: A charge of murder is held without bail until the case is disposed of; the rest are bailed after bail_days (Part 2 step 5).

heat.why: An arrest of a man writes investigative and public heat on his organisations, as a share of the package's own_full and city_full heat figures, the public part scaled by the report's publicity (unsourced).

disposition.why: A case that ends in an arrest runs on to a disposition weighed from the evidence, a lawyer, money, witness pressure and the Pad. B13 keeps a minimal version; prison phase 1 replaces it with a package-defined stage graph.
disposition.days_why: Days from arrest to disposition: murder cases take most of a year, street assaults a season (unsourced).

dismiss.why: z of a charge dropped or dismissed: a weak case, a good lawyer, a bought officer and frightened witnesses push it up; a loud case pushes it down. B13b: bias lowered from 0.5 to 0 after a run showed 40% of dispositions dismissed; from memory (approximate) roughly a quarter to a third of 1970s felony arrests were dismissed or dropped. A target, never a cap.

trial.why: z of going to trial rather than pleading: a strong case pleads, a loud case and a good lawyer go to trial, and a made man typically refuses to plead if it means naming others (Part II 6.5). B13b: bias lowered from -1.2 to -2.0 after a run showed 17% of dispositions going to verdict; from memory (approximate) about nine in ten convictions were by plea. A target, never a cap.

conviction.why: z of a guilty verdict at trial (unsourced).

disposition.witness_pressure_why: Witness pressure = the share of witnesses (the witness driver) times the offender's organisations' violence and investigative heat against the package's own_full.

sentence.term_days_why: Median term imposed, in days (20 years for murder, 18 months for an assault; unsourced), spread lognormally. Not caps.
sentence.factors_why: A plea earns 0.6 of the term; publicity adds up to 0.4 of it and a killed officer 0.5 (unsourced).
sentence.parole_why: The earliest release day is start + term * parole_share: eligibility after about a third of the term (New Jersey practice, from memory, to be checked). A man is returned on that day.

facilities.why: Part II 8: the county jail holds the unsentenced and short sentences; Ironhaven the state felons for long terms; federal prisoners go to penitentiaries in other states. Which penitentiary is Open (the bible); free text here.

backing.why: A head or unit leader of a man who is arrested weighs sending a lawyer or waiting (Part 2 step 7).

lawyer_fee.why: A defence lawyer's retainer for a felony in 1975 dollars (unsourced).

backing.lawyer_half_fee_why: The fee at which the lawyer is half as good as the best (fee/(fee+half)); unsourced.
backing.trust_why: The head's trust in a man held on a homicide charge falls by a seeded 0 to 10 (a worry about who talks; Part 2 step 7).
